newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 18.

text.p: - Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- BROWN STICKS TO EMU ENTRY DATE

Gordon Brown, shadow chancellor with Labour, is reported to have stressed that his party would still aim to take Britain into the single currency at its inception, despite the new Labour policy of supporting the holding of a referendum on the issue. Observers, however, view the commitment to a referendum as reducing the chances of the UK being among the first participants in Emu on January 1 1999. The move has prompted Tory Eurosceptics to demand the party more clearly distinguish its policy from that of Labour on the issue.
-- PRIVATE SECTOR MAY TAKE OVER TRAFFIC CONTROL

It is reported that a number of private sector companies are to be asked to establish up to five regional traffic control centres for England. The centres, to be set under the private finance initiative, would assume responsibility for traffic control from the police. The government believes that there are considerable financial savings to be made in centralising the current system for managing traffic levels.
-- DEUTSCHE TELEKOM SHARES GET CAUTIOUS PRICING

Deutsche Telekom, which will list on the stock exchange on Monday, is to pitch its share price at DM28.50, a level well below the previously indicated DM30. The decision is seen as an attempt by the company and its bankers, Goldman Sachs and Deutsche Bank, to avoid any market backlash. Two-thirds of the massive flotation of shares will go to private investors in Germany, with approximately 14 per cent going to the US and another 8 per cent to British investors. The IPO is expected to raise DM20 billion.
-- ROW DELAYS FIRST CHINESE LISTING ON LONDON EXCHANGE

The planned listing of the first Chinese company on the London Stock Exchange is reported to have run into problems over the pricing of shares in Beijing Datang Power Generation. Bankers involved in the flotation, Salomon Brothers and Kleinwort Benson, have failed to reach an agreement on a suitable pricing for the issue, which had been planning to raise 181.8 million stg in both London and Hong Kong.
-- BAe KNOCKED OUT OF US FIGHTER COMPETITION

It has been revealed that a consortium involving British Aerospace, McDonnell Douglas and Northrop Grumman will not be considered for the contract to build a new range of fighter aircraft for the US and Britain, the Joint Strike Fighter (JSF). Instead the competition will now be between Boeing and Lockheed Martin. Final selection of which company will develop and manufacture the new strike aircraft is expected to be made by the end of the decade. The decision to eliminate BAe and its two US partners is being seen as a major blow to the group.
-- NORTHERN ELECTRIC TO REVEAL ITS DEFENCE AGAINST CALENERGY
BID

Details are expected to be announced today by Northern Electric of its defence against a hostile 766 million stg takeover bid from US power group CalEnergy. The company will stress that the bid is too low and that initially CalEnergy had appeared to be willing to pay more for the group. The defence will also point to the potential worth of its 8 per cent stake in the telecoms venture Ionica. Meanwhile, there are rumours that further bids in the UK energy sector are in the offing.
-- ELECTRONIC MONEY THREAT TO BANKS

The Bank for International Settlements has issued a warning to banks that they face losing a significant amount of revenue if customers decide to switch from traditional cash to electronic alternatives. The warning relates to the development of smartcards on which digital cash can be loaded, allowing the holder to carry out purchases. Central banks, the BIS notes, might need to consider placing a value on the issuing of electronic cash as a means of offsetting the impact of a decline in the number of banknotes.
-- EUROPEAN PC SALES RISE 12 PER CENT IN THIRD QUARTER

During the third quarter sales in Europe of personal computers rose 12.4 per cent to 3.44 million units, according to figures from Dataquest. The figure represents a major improvement on the figure of 6.7 per cent growth during the second quarter, though remains well below the 1995 first quarter figure of 30 per cent. Sales in Germany rose during the period by 14.7 per cent, while in the UK the figure was 17.4 per cent. Compaq remained the leader in the field, with a slightly reduced market share of 12.9 per cent.
-- QATAR WEAPONS DEAL FOR UK

Britain has signed a deal to provide 500 million stg in weapons systems to the Arab state of Qatar. The contract involves the provision of Hawk jet training aircraft, armoured personnel carriers, missiles and patrol boats. Companies providing the hardware include British Aerospace, GKN, Vosper Thornycroft and Shorts. The news comes in the wake of a deal to supply Australia with one billion sterling worth of Hawk trainers. The UK is also competing to secure a contract with Qatar for 50 main battle tanks.
-- JOBLESS TOTAL SET TO MEET EU TARGET

A report due to be published next month by the European Commission is expected to indicate that the UK will be the only EU member state to reach a target of reducing unemployment by half by the year 2000. This aim was a key objective of the former European Commission president Jacques Delors and will be seen by the British government as a vindication of its commitment to free labour markets. The report, however, is also expected to calculate that a national minimum wage would not impact adversely on employment. For a full range of news monitoring services, phone BMC +44-171-377-1742
